neighbours.label: the word rouse/arouse in any form (rouse, roused, rousing, arouse, arousing, arousal), read on the word itself, plus the spelling look-alike 'carouse'; more weakly the noun 'opening' (a job opening, an opening in the defense); quiet on other -ouse look-alikes (house, mouse, grouse, trousers, Rousseau) and on same-meaning words without it (stir, wake, excite, provoke)
fire: The sailors liked to carouse in the harbor bars.
The alarm failed to rouse the sleeping guard.
She was roused from her nap by the sound of thunder.
The coach gave a rousing speech before the final match.
His strange behavior began to arouse suspicion among the neighbors.
The documentary aims to arouse public interest in ocean conservation.
Caffeine increases physiological arousal and alertness in most people.
After the victory, the soldiers went out to carouse until dawn.
quiet: He would grouse about the weather all day.
The alarm failed to wake the sleeping guard.
She was woken from her nap by the sound of thunder.
The coach gave a stirring speech before the final match.
His strange behavior began to provoke questions among the neighbors.
The documentary aims to spark public interest in ocean conservation.
Caffeine increases alertness and focus in most people.
After the victory, the soldiers went back to the house until dawn.
